scenario: AITA for not helping a woman at walmart | I (male 24) started working at walmart for the summer about a month ago. My job mainly involves working with inventory in the back room and not on the floor with customers, sometimes we get heavy boxes that we need to lift as a part of our regular duties. One of my co-workers is a female (fcw) in her early to mid 30s, physically in good shape and as far as I can tell no physical disabilities. (Fcw) approaches me and asks if I can help her lift a heavy box, I say of course and I walk over to the box with her expecting us to perform a team lift - however we get to the box and as I get to one side of the box expecting her to go to the other she just stands there and watches me. I ask "are you ready?" And she says "yes it just needs to go in that bin" (referencing a metal shelving unit about 4 feet high). I say "ok let's do it" and she responds "it's to heavy for me can you please lift it into the bin?". I respond by saying "I'm more than happy to help anyone if they're having trouble with something, but I'm not going to lift all your heavy boxes for you while you stand there watching me" and (fcw) said "if you're not willing to help me I'll find someone who will" and stormed off. Later on the head guy on our team (not my boss just the guy with most seniority who directs us) walks up to me and said " I just spoke to (fcw), the next time someone asks for help you need to help them, that's part of being a team. I responded by clarifying exactly what happened in case she stretched the truth and finished by saying "we're both paid to do the exact same job and if she cant perform the tasks then she shouldn't have taken the job, I'm not the designated heavy lifter on our team and if you would like to discuss this further we can do it with HR present", and at this point feeling pretty annoyed, it was my turn to storm off. So, was I the asshole in this situation? Because so far it seems like its 2 against 1.

By balancing these considerations, the couple can effectively use a registry while respecting their mom's perspective and ensuring guests feel appreciated.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I was the asshole in this situation at Walmart. Let me start by going through what happened step by step to understand my actions and the reactions of others. First, I started working at Walmart for the summer about a month ago. My job is mainly in the back room dealing with inventory, which involves lifting heavy boxes. One of my co-workers is a woman in her early to mid-30s, who seems physically fit and doesn't have any obvious disabilities. She approached me and asked if I could help her lift a heavy box. I agreed, thinking we'd do a team lift. But when we got to the box, she just stood there watching me instead of helping. I asked if she was ready, and she said it just needed to go into a bin that's about 4 feet high. I offered to help, but she said it was too heavy for her and asked me to lift it into the bin alone. I responded that I'm happy to help if she's having trouble, but I'm not going to lift all her heavy boxes while she stands there. She got upset and stormed off. Later, the head guy on our team talked to me about the incident. He said that the next time someone asks for help, I need to help them because that's part of being a team. I clarified what happened, explaining that I wasn't willing to do all her heavy lifting while she watched. I also mentioned that both of us are paid to do the same job, and if she can't perform the tasks, she shouldn't have taken the job. I suggested that if he wanted to discuss it further, we could involve HR. Feeling annoyed, I stormed off. So, the question is: Was I the asshole in this situation? It seems like it's two against one, with the co-worker and the head guy against me. Let me think about this. On one hand, I was willing to help her lift the box, but I expected her to help too since we're both supposed to be doing the same job. It seemed unfair that she wanted me to do all the work while she watched. On the other hand, she might have felt that she needed help and was asking for it, and my refusal could have come off as uncooperative or dismissive. Also, the head guy's perspective is that helping each other is part of being a team, which makes sense in a workplace setting. But I felt that I was being asked to do more than my share of the work, especially since we're both paid to do the same tasks. I wonder if there's a middle ground here. Maybe I could have communicated my willingness to help in a way that still respected her need for assistance without feeling like I was being taken advantage of. Perhaps suggesting that we work together on lifting the box instead of her standing by could have been a better approach. Additionally, storming off after the head guy talked to me might have escalated the situation. Maybe staying calm and open to discussion would have been better, even if I felt annoyed. Overall, I think my intention was to be fair and not take on more work than my share, but my approach might have come off as uncooperative or dismissive. The head guy's perspective emphasizes teamwork, which is important in any workplace, so perhaps I could have found a way to balance both my concerns and the team's needs. In the end, it's a bit of a gray area. I wasn't entirely in the wrong for wanting to share the workload, but my communication and reaction could have been handled differently to maintain better team dynamics.
